text:
cheng: heads up — production deploys to GPU pool failed ~2m ago with `403 Forbidden` from the deploy controller, looks related to KMS envelope rotation logs showing `access denied` for service-account-controller.
maria: saw the alert, diggin in. which namespace was impacted?
cheng: `inference-prod` and the autoscaler namespace. multiple jobs hit `CreatePod` perm denied.
alex: deploy-bot just posted an incident: `INC-20260321-172` created for RBAC/KMS access failures :warning:.
deploy-bot: [automated] Incident INC-20260321-172 opened by deploy-monitor. severity=P2. linked runbooks: /runbooks/gpu-access-403.md
sam: quick theory — we rolled the KMS proxy cert yesterday and the key-wrap role mapping may have lost `kms:Decrypt` on the helm-deploy SA. checking KMS audit logs now.
maria: KMS logs show `Decrypt` attempts for envelope ids 0x3a... all returned 403 with principal `system:serviceaccount:platform:helm-deploy`.
cheng: that matches. but why also `system:serviceaccount:infra:node-provisioner` failed? did the role binding scope change?
olivia: I pushed the RBAC slimdown two days ago (refactor: move cluster-level deploy bindings to ns-scoped ones). suspect a gap where cross-namespace SAs needed cluster-scoped binding for KMS wrapper.
alex: can we hotfix by re-adding a narrowly scoped ClusterRoleBinding that only grants `kms:Decrypt` via `kms-wrapper` clusterrole to two SAs? we should avoid broad cluster-admin.
sam: agreed. proposed minimal ClusterRole: name `kms-encrypt-decrypt-wrapper` with rules for `kms:Decrypt` via impersonation subject list: `serviceAccount:platform:helm-deploy`, `serviceAccount:infra:node-provisioner`. quick patch applied in staging, testing now.
maria: while patching, I noticed audit logs lacked the `k8s.amazon.com/requester` field for some KMS proxy calls — our KMS-proxy didn't forward annotation context after RBAC change. that will make postmortem hard. we need to add structured audit forwarding.
cheng: urgent: patch approved. sam — can you run `kubectl apply -f -` with the CRB YAML and post output?
sam: running now: ```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: kms-encrypt-decrypt-wrapper
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: kms-wrapper
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: helm-deploy
  namespace: platform
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: node-provisioner
  namespace: infra
```
apply result: `clusterrolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/kms-encrypt-decrypt-wrapper created`
alex: nice. any immediate deploys succeeding?
cheng: I retriggered a canary deploy — pod created, kubelet pulled image, GPU assigned. no more 403s for the canary.
maria: good. next: we need to schedule a proper least-privilege rollout so we don't keep this CRB forever. options: 1) add namespace-scoped RoleBindings + trust proxy that maps SA->kms principal per-namespace, 2) update KMS-proxy to accept pod/serviceaccount scoping via annotation and validate.
olivia: option 2 is better long-term, but more work. for short-term we should: create a ticket to audit all SAs that need cross-namespace KMS wrap and add them to a narrowly scoped allowlist, then expire the CRB after 72h with automation.
security-oncall: capturing actions: 1) hotfix CRB applied (sam) 2) add audit-forwarding to KMS-proxy (maria) 3) run SA access audit across clusters (olivia) 4) schedule POD-level KMS principal mapping RFC (cheng). I'll file a high-priority GH issue and link to INC-20260321-172.
sam: also dropping a short-term mitigator: add a `predeploy` check in the deploy pipeline to assert SA has `kms:Decrypt` via `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:... decrypt` for target SA. quick lint to avoid footguns.
alex: +1. can we add an alert rule for KMS-proxy 5xx/403 spike tied to GPU pool scale failures?
maria: on it. I will add a monitoring rule and increase retention for KMS audit logs for 30d.
olch: small note — please remove the CRB after 72h or when the RFC lands, whichever is first. add a scheduled job to auto-delete if not needed.
cheng: thanks team. I will do the postmortem doc tomorrow with timeline, root cause (RBAC slimming + KMS-proxy annotation loss), and follow-ups. tagging @oncall-sre for visibility. :spiral_notepad:
security-oncall: we should also notify compliance — there was an access-denied pattern affecting customer workloads, might be review-worthy.
alex: copying compliance and legal in a separate thread.
maria: incident resolved for now, keeping monitoring on.
sam: leaving the CRB in place and will add the auto-expire job.
cheng: closing thread here, moving actions to GH and INC. thanks all :thumbsup:
